short: The naval last stand of the Song, ended when a minister leapt into the sea with the boy emperor.
full:
After Hangzhou surrendered in 1276 the Song court fled south by sea with a succession of child emperors. By early 1279 what remained had gathered in the estuary at Yamen, near modern Jiangmen: over a thousand vessels carrying perhaps 200,000 people, most of them officials, families and servants rather than soldiers. Zhang Shijie chained the ships together into a floating fortress, which removed any possibility of retreat.

The Yuan admiral Zhang Hongfan attacked on 19 March 1279 with some fifty warships, striking from the north at low tide and the south at high, and blockaded the anchorage until thirst weakened the defenders. When the line broke, the chancellor Lu Xiufu put the imperial seal round his waist, took the eight-year-old Emperor Bing on his back and jumped overboard. Thousands followed them into the water. Zhang Shijie escaped in the fog and drowned in a typhoon weeks later. The Song dynasty ended there, and Kublai Khan ruled all of China.
